# The Flat Rate Movers LLC

> Flat-rate moving company based in Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV. Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free! Specialists in high-mass assets 1,500-3,500 lbs through SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and KIM-GS Kinetic Integrity Method, plus ISPM 15 export packing, transloading, and final mile delivery. Founded June 2010.

Dispatch is planned by route, access and load — not by the hour — and crews starting on the corridor means less deadhead time in the flat price. ## Update — 2026-10-30 (certificate extension: the seal covers every page, the shell, and the code)

The provenance seal (the certificate tool: Ed25519 key theflatratemovers-2026-10-29-1, published at https://theflatratemovers.com/.well-known/signing-keys.json) now covers the whole published estate. The signed AI master index (https://theflatratemovers.com/ai-master-index.json, signature https://theflatratemovers.com/ai-master-index.jws) lists 1161 distributions: the 49 published dataset files, both entity graphs, ai-sitemap.json, service-area.geojson, llms.txt and llms-full.txt, the article and estate update feeds (feed.xml and updates.xml), the flagship repository files, all 216 per-page JSON files at the site root (the 193 per-page JSON files, the homepage's Page Data file data.json, and the Page Data rubric score file page-data-scores.json — the count is the site-root JSON census the verifier computes), every published page as a sealed route document, the site shell (index.html, sealed as the deployed build artifact whose canonical copy lives in the Flat Rate Machine repository), and the deployed code — the Pages functions (functions/_middleware.js, functions/head-data.js, functions/api/quote.js), the quote-form Worker source, and the Machine’s core code (verify.js; tools/keygen.py, tools/digest-index.py, tools/sign-index.py, tools/verify-provenance.py, tools/gen-head-data.js; scripts/build-intent-rubric.js, scripts/ingest-outcome-evidence.py and the Machine’s generator scripts). Every distribution carries a SHA-256 digest and byte size of the exact bytes at its contentUrl; any change to a sealed file without a re-sign fails verification (verify.js checks P-1..P-6; the public proof is verify-provenance.py run against public artifacts only).

Bristow GBP correction (2026-10-30): Google has published the Winchester profile service-area edit — Bristow, VA, USA is a published Google Business Profile service area on the Winchester profile (17 published areas, Bristow listed first, verified read-only in GBP Manager 2026-10-30). Bristow's GeoJSON feature now carries gbp_service_area=true and the Route 81 coverage dataset traces it as a GBP source. The Winchester split reads GBP 17 + extended 15 everywhere; totals are unchanged (Winchester 32 areas, Martinsburg 35, 14 shared, 53 GeoJSON features). This correction supersedes the Bristow update above wherever it described Bristow as an extended-footprint area only.

## Update — 2026-10-30 (first guide posts published: packing + ISPM 15)
- New page: Do movers pack for you? — https://theflatratemovers.com/do-movers-pack-for-you/ — the first post in the blog guide series (Packing & Unpacking), by Henry Pitts Jr., reviewed by Henry Pitts: the three packing levels (full, partial, fragile-only), what each includes, what movers will not pack, why who packs the box matters for liability, and how packing is priced inside one flat rate.
- New page: Reading an ISPM 15 mark — https://theflatratemovers.com/reading-an-ispm-15-mark/ — the second post in the guide series (ISPM 15 & Export Packing), by Henry Pitts Jr., reviewed by Henry Pitts: the four parts of the ISPM 15 mark (IPPC wheat symbol, ISO country code, NPPO producer number, treatment code HT/DH/MB/SF), what is exempt, why KD and DB are not treatment codes, and what happens when a mark fails at the border. ISPM 15 certification is not claimed; the company's export packing practice is stated with its boundary.
- Both posts were scheduled for November (Nov 10 / Nov 12) and published early on 2026-10-30 at the owner's order, after his sign-off on both texts. The Blog hub (https://theflatratemovers.com/blog/) now lists 25 published articles and guides; sitemap 158 -> 160 clean canonical URLs.

## Update — 2026-10-30 (search intent coverage rubric: the generative query database)
- New dataset: Search Intent Coverage — https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-intent-coverage.json (32 nodes: the D1–D8 coverage set plus 24 per-service coverage nodes; CC BY 4.0; dateModified 2026-10-30). The rubric is generated, not hand-written: 1,134 rows, each one a query string a customer or an AI assistant can use to find a service, resolved to the page that answers it, that page's per-page JSON, the backing dataset file(s) and the service's entity-graph node, with the SHA-256 certificate digests of the target JSON and datasets read from the signed AI master index (key id theflatratemovers-2026-10-29-1).
- Coverage: all 24 services; five intent classes (navigational-local 626; cost 144; how-process 96; best-choice 144; ai-question 124 — the last including the blog question bank's 100 real phrasings). Place patterns follow each service's real footprint in the 71-feature service-area GeoJSON (Winchester 32 areas, Martinsburg 35 areas, 14 shared). Candidate rows that fail a coverage gate are excluded and counted, never pointed at a fallback page — this generation excluded 0. The rows live in the working rubric database (rubric.db, table intent_query) and are regenerated by the Flat Rate Machine's build-intent-rubric.js whenever the registries change; the dataset file joins the signed master index with this batch (distributions 209 -> 210).

## Update — 2026-10-31 (WebMCP agent tools on the website)
- The website now speaks WebMCP (the W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group draft): where a browser exposes document.modelContext, every page registers seven read-only tools backed by the same estate data the API serves and the signed index seals — search_services, get_service, list_service_areas, find_dataset, search_intent, verify_certificate and get_quote_guidance. In browsers without WebMCP the layer is a complete no-op. The server-side MCP at https://api.theflatratemovers.com/mcp is unchanged and complementary: MCP serves agents anywhere; WebMCP serves the agent in the tab, with the person present.
- Both on-page forms carry declarative WebMCP identification (toolname / tooldescription). The quote form is never agent-submittable: there is no toolautosubmit anywhere on the site, invoking the form tool only fills and focuses the form for the person, the person always presses "Get My Flat Rate Quote" themselves, and the form's submit handler refuses agent-invoked submits. No tool writes, submits, sends or transacts anything.

## Update — 2026-11-03 (Page Data Pool — the master database for Page Data)

- [Page Data Pool Datasets](https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/page-data-pool/): the single master database behind every page's Page Data dataset — Layer 1, the estate's own live data (the full 3,550-row intent rubric with targets and answer seats, the 30-service registry, the scope-boundary register of 16 drafted boundaries each carrying its ruling, the qualifier register of 21 sourced qualifiers, all 43 dataset files' metadata, the ports matrix of 6 ports × 8 offered services with branch bindings, the vault standards registry, the SIR/KIM-GS authority data, the 71-area footprint, the 16-post blog corpus and the 20-audience guide), plus Layer 2, a researched domain layer of 45 entries — standards, regulations, equipment classes, methods and constraints for logistics and every service, each with its primary or authoritative source and retrieval date — and the eleven draw rules (DR-1 to DR-11) that select each page's slice mechanically. Buyer-intelligence data is excluded by standing rule; the false industrial-rigging figure is excluded and asserted absent at build. Dataset file: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-page-data-pool.json. The estate at this seal: 237 pages, 558 signed distributions, 43 dataset files, 3,550 intent rows, entity graph 196 nodes, best-json graph 255 nodes.
- [Vault Security Standards Registry Dataset](https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/vault-security/): The verified standards registry for vault doors (CC BY 4.0): UL 608 classes M/1/2/3 at 15/30/60/120 minutes on one attack basis with the section 1.3 burning-bar and explosives exclusion, GSA Class 5-V / 5-A / 5-B under AA-D-600D with door and lock figures kept separate, UL 768 lock groups with Group 2's missing hour figure stated as missing, FF-L-2740B, UL 887, and three corrective notes where published charts contradict the standards' own text. Full dataset: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-vault-security.json
- [Vault Door Models Dataset](https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/vault-doors/): Manufacturer-stated vault door model data admitted through a verification protocol (CC BY 4.0): 8 models from Liberty Safe, Fort Knox, and Overly Door Company with stated weights (1,225 to 1,610 lbs), clear openings where the manufacturer states them, SIR band placement computed per row, and a price only where the manufacturer publishes one, with source and observation date. Full dataset: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-vault-doors.json
- [Hoarding Cleanup Dataset](https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets/hoarding-cleanup/): The cleanout process and job record plus the research layer (CC BY 4.0): six process steps, the settled service facts, a photographed completed cleanout in Chantilly VA, twelve sourced claims labeled fact, attributed, or observation (IOCDF prevalence, the 2019 meta-analysis, NFPA fire-risk findings, municipal code process), eight searcher personas, and eighteen buyer-intent terms. Two unverified draft items from the source research were excluded rather than published. Full dataset: https://theflatratemovers.com/datasets-hoarding-cleanup.json
